item: Which equipment, site or upgrade set off the overload, and whether L3Harris FTI was involved
note: Partly answered Saturday. At the 10:30 AM ET DOT briefing, Duffy said the outage began during L3Harris copper-to-fiber work at a remote FAA site, when a router involved in the work flooded the network. Still open: which site, whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred (officials have not determined it), any written FAA report, and L3Harris's account of the fault. L3Harris has now responded in writing: it is supporting the FAA investigation and says more than 70% of the copper-to-fiber conversion is done, but it does not address the router ([L3Harris statement](https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/press-release/2026/11/l3harris-statement-nov-13-ground-stop)). DOT's written release of Duffy's remarks adds that the router made over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds ([DOT release](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/icymi-us-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-provides-update-restoration-airspace)). Reuters (via CNA), citing officials, reports possible router problems in both Arkansas and Texas and 17 of 22 en route centers affected (Reported). CBS (update caused a reboot) and Bloomberg (FBI looking at a software update; equipment already over capacity) stay Reported. [Yahoo News](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/live/faa-ground-stop-latest-updates-duffy-blames-contractor-l3harris-thousands-more-flights-canceled-saturday-no-sign-of-cyberattack-161329174.html) · [AInvest](https://www.ainvest.com/news/duffy-contractor-l3harris-working-telecommunication-maintenance-time-time-aviation-shutdown-2611/) Sunday check (8:14 AM ET): the WSJ (via Investing.com) reports the sites as an FAA radio facility in El Dorado, Ark., and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, with a newly installed Juniper router involved and first trouble at Indianapolis Center; HPE says its devices did not fail (Reported). The PASS union says two routers updated Friday were involved (Reported). Bedford confirmed on the record that the FAA is swapping about 2,000 Cisco 600 routers for Juniper routers as routine work, without saying which router failed. Still no written FAA root-cause report. [Investing.com (citing WSJ)](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/faa-router-overload-in-arkansas-triggered-nationwide-flight-grounding--wsj-5027664) · [Magnolia Reporter](https://www.magnoliareporter.com/news_and_business/union_county/article_14de6a8d-c040-442b-a7ff-578db41b1c7e.html) · [Herald Business](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10937583) · [DOT release](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/icymi-us-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-provides-update-restoration-airspace) Sunday 5:16 PM ET: the FAA's written Q&A now names the two sites on the record (Amarillo, Texas, radar site; El Dorado, Ark., radio site, where L3Harris was deploying a new router) and says root cause is still under investigation; the routers are in L3Harris's Florida lab. Still open: faulty router vs. installation or configuration, and a final root-cause report. [FAA Q&A](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/nationwide-ground-stop-questions-and-answers) · [DOT Sunday release](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/icymi-trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-provides-update-across-sunday) Monday 10:25 AM ET: still no written root cause. The routers are in L3Harris's Florida lab with FAA, Juniper and Cisco engineers (Duffy's X post via Fox News, Reported). Duffy says the Amarillo router was replaced about three weeks earlier and began flooding when the El Dorado router was switched on (DOT release, Confirmed). HPE says the device "functioned as it was configured to by the installer" (via ABC, Reported). Open: installer/configuration error vs. faulty router, and why both sites flooded at once. [DOT Sunday release](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/icymi-trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-provides-update-across-sunday) · [ABC News live updates](https://abcnews.com/US/live-updates/faa-ground-stop-live-updates-hundreds-flights-canceled/?entryId=138163207&id=138125140) · [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/us/duffy-investigators-examining-2-routers-nationwide-faa-ground-stop-no-signs-foreign-cyberattack)

item: Cause of the frequency and radar problems
note: Named at a high level by officials. Duffy said on record that legacy analog TDM switches and routers carrying voice and radar data were overloaded with data and gave inconsistent data from 3:36 PM ET, so the FAA shut the system down; Mullin said new equipment overwhelmed the older system. The NBC "instability" and "didn't lose all radar" wording is now backed by Reuters and Aviation Week. No vendor, site or specific upgrade has been named; see the new open item. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/3fec1b0a85a0/world/us/faa-issues-national-ground-stop-due-extraordinary-circumstance-reasons-safety-2026-11-13/) · [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqx2wyvyr3zzo) · [Los Angeles Times](https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2026-11-13/what-caused-national-ground-stop-here-is-what-we-know) · [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/air-transport/safety-ops-regulation/faa-lifts-nationwide-ground-stop-points-data-overload-cause)

item: Why O'Hare is ground stopped again after the national cancel
note: At 8:59 PM ET the FAA summary lists the Advisory 011 O'Hare stop as 2nd tier, UAL and subsidiaries only, reason OTHER / AIRLINE REQUEST, until 9:45 PM ET. It is a United-requested hold, not a new FAA equipment stop. [FAA NAS summary](https://www.fly.faa.gov/ois/oisedit/summary_pub)

item: Confirm the CBS network-update/reboot report with the FAA or DOT
note: Checked 7:22 PM ET and rechecked as of 8:52 PM ET, including the Duffy/Mullin briefing: not confirmed. FAA and DOT still call it a telecommunications or communication outage; the FAA newsroom still says "communication issues." The briefing coverage reviewed does not quote either official confirming a reboot, a software update, or naming L3Harris. CBS, citing unnamed multiple sources, reports an update to the L3Harris-operated ATC network caused a reboot and crash; that stays Reported/unconfirmed. Bloomberg, at 5:01 PM ET, citing one unnamed person, says the FBI is looking at a software update and does not believe it was a cyberattack. No vendor or product is named. The FBI has not commented, and no independent corroboration was found (only re-reports). The CBS and Bloomberg accounts are compatible but are separate claims. CNN, via Fox 5 Vegas, reports the FAA told airlines the problem began with network routers, possibly at Chicago Midway; that is unconfirmed. CISA, the FBI and L3Harris have made no public statement as of 8:52 PM ET.

item: Which specific frequencies or channels went down
note: None named publicly; a unique Reagan National tower failure remains unconfirmed. A facility-level NOTAM search was blocked or required a login and was not completed. No public advisory or restriction names a failed circuit or frequency.

note: Cancelled at 8:16 PM ET by FAA Advisory 005 (signed 8:19 PM ET), destination ALL, facilities ALL, with no reason given and the next update at 11 PM ET. item: Whether the Newark PENNS restriction clears with the national stop
note: No longer on the FAA restrictions list at 9:21 PM ET, ahead of its listed midnight end; no reason was published. Earlier: still listed until midnight ET and has now outlasted the national stop, which was cancelled at 8:16 PM ET. Official FAA text is STOP ZOB to EWR via PENNS 2234-0500 EQ:FAA (Cleveland Center traffic arriving at Newark via PENNS, not Newark departures); requested by ZNY and provided by ZOB, started 5:34 PM ET. That is consistent with a separate Cleveland-to-Newark restriction but is not proof of a second fault. Still listed at 8:59 PM ET. [FAA restrictions list](https://www.fly.faa.gov/restrictions/restrictions?reqFac=ALL&provFac=ALL)

item: What "communications failure" means in practice
note: Per Duffy: the TDM (time-division multiplexing) system, mostly copper lines that carry ATC voice and radar data, whose switches and routers were overloaded; radar and communications became intermittent but were never fully lost. [Los Angeles Times](https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2026-11-13/what-caused-national-ground-stop-here-is-what-we-know) · [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/3fec1b0a85a0/world/us/faa-issues-national-ground-stop-due-extraordinary-circumstance-reasons-safety-2026-11-13/)

item: Rumor that AT&T provides the ARTCC network
note: Partly true at most. AT&T won the FENS contract in Aug 2026, but the only funded work is a $74.3M planning task order. L3Harris still operates FTI. No recent public document names AT&T as a current FTI circuit provider, and nothing public links AT&T to today's outage.

item: Rumor that 911 systems are also down
note: Unconfirmed. No FCC, carrier or 911-center confirmation of a nationwide outage. Downdetector logged user reports from 4:13 PM ET (unverified, likely including panic reports) and a separate overnight spike (peak 298 at about 5:21 AM ET). Lincoln, NE and Tulare, CA lost only non-emergency lines; Lincoln-Lancaster EMA said 911 was working.

item: Any SMART link to the outage
note: Mullin said on the record that CISA is "looking at" a possible link to the FAA's SMART AI tool ([GeekWire](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/dhs-chief-sees-no-microsoft-link-to-faa-ground-stop-says-possible-ai-role-being-investigated/)); that statement is confirmed. Any actual SMART role remains unconfirmed. Air Space Intelligence has denied that SMART caused the outage (on the record, via GeekWire). AvWeb quotes Duffy saying SMART is not connected to STARS or ERAM and that "There's no possible way SMART would have impacted what happened." Reuters still has Mullin saying a rogue AI is not fully ruled out, so this stays open. [AvWeb](https://avweb.com/aviation-news/faa-nationwide-ground-stop-lifts-smart-ai/)

item: Chicago as the starting point
note: First in the FAA paperwork, confirmed. Whether the failure technically started there is still unclear. The Air Current, citing airline sources, reports the outage was first reported at Chicago Center, then Boston, Washington, New York and Minneapolis in rapid succession, after which the FAA went nationwide. That sequence is reported, not an official center-by-center log. [The Air Current](https://theaircurrent.com/feed/dispatches/u-s-halts-flight-departures-nationwide-on-air-traffic-communications-outage/)

item: L3Harris copper-to-fiber changeover as the cause
note: The 70% upgraded figure is confirmed. A cutover causing today's outage is unverified: no public schedule or contract change names Nov. 13, and L3Harris says it cuts over in low-traffic windows.

item: Cleveland Center equipment hold on Newark arrivals
note: The restriction is still listed until midnight ET and has now outlasted the national stop cancelled at 8:16 PM ET. That is consistent with a separate Cleveland-to-Newark restriction but is not proof of a second fault. Official FAA restrictions list: STOP ZOB to EWR via PENNS 2234-0500 EQ:FAA — Cleveland Center traffic arriving at Newark via PENNS, not Newark departures. Requested by ZNY, provided by ZOB, 5:34 PM–midnight ET. Earlier Newark stops were for volume and ended before 3:10 PM. Recheck at midnight ET.

item: The two areas that kept communicating
note: Mullin said two US areas were unaffected and would not name them. Inference, medium confidence: Alaska and Hawaii, based on Alaska Airlines' statement that intra-Alaska and Neighbor Island flights were not impacted. No FAA advisory carves them out.

item: Cyberattack
note: Monday: no FBI or CISA public statement or finding found. The FAA Q&A says it has "no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor"; Duffy says the FBI offered assistance and he will share anything it finds. [FAA Q&A](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/nationwide-ground-stop-questions-and-answers) · [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/16/cyberattack-faa-ground-stop-sean-duffy-l3harris-fiber-installation-arkansas/) At the 8:35 PM ET briefing, Mullin said there was "no cyberattack" (ABC, NBC, BBC). NBC quotes him adding, "So far what we've seen there is no cyberattack. We're still working through that process." Earlier in the afternoon he would not rule a cyberattack out. CISA and the FBI have made no public statement as of 8:50 PM ET. Bloomberg, citing one unnamed person, had earlier said the FBI does not think it was a cyberattack. A verification pass found no independent corroboration of that Bloomberg report, and the FBI itself has not commented.

item: Kansas City Center as the origin, and Reagan National
note: The Kansas City origin is a rumor, contradicted by the Chicago-first advisories. No ZKC-specific advisory. Reagan National held under the national stop is confirmed. A unique tower failure is unconfirmed.

item: Why the Weather Service radar site went down
note: Debunked as a nationwide NWS/NEXRAD or radar.weather.gov outage. Stale Los Angeles office page text; NWS, NCEP, and NWS Birmingham/Huntsville say radar and dataflow are normal. Narrower confirmed TDWR dropouts at Newark, Milwaukee and a Boston airport weather-radar feed are documented in the timeline and are not a national Weather Service outage.

item: Canadian systems hit
note: Not hit, per NAV CANADA and Transport Minister MacKinnon. Only US-bound flights, and some flights crossing US airspace, were stopped.

item: Airport weather radar dropouts tied to the same network
note: Confirmed brief Friday dropouts at Newark (TEWR, 12:19–12:44 PM ET) and Milwaukee (TMKE, 12:46–3:53 PM ET) terminal Doppler weather radars. Boston Center's telecom issue was cited when Boston's airport weather-radar feed came back at 3:46 PM ET. These are airport TDWR feeds, not a nationwide NWS/NEXRAD outage.

item: Public carrier outage ruled out for the window
note: No public AT&T or Verizon consumer outage lines up with the window. L3Harris runs the private FTI network and had no comment.
